claim: Enhancers are DNA elements, typically a few hundred base pairs long, that bind transcription factors (TFs) and boost the activity of genes in cis.
source: Enhancers are DNA elements, typically a few hundred base pairs long, that bind transcription factors (TFs) and boost the activity of genes in cis (Banerji et al., 1981).
evidence: Supported by citation to Banerji et al., 1981

claim: Two-way combinatorial MPRA studies that tested a large number of enhancer-promoter pairs revealed a variable degree of intrinsic compatibility between enhancers and promoters.
source: Among others, two-way combinatorial MPRA studies that tested a large number of enhancer-promoter pairs revealed a variable degree of intrinsic compatibility between enhancers and promoters (Zabidi et al., 2015; Bergman et al., 2022; Martinez-Ara et al., 2022), in line with earlier evidence from analyses of single genomic loci (Bertolino and Singh, 2002; Chang et al., 2004; Vakoc et al., 2005; Jing et al., 2008; Deng et al., 2012).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations to previous studies

claim: Surveys of mammalian genomes suggest that there are many more enhancers than genes.
source: Surveys of mammalian genomes suggest that there are many more enhancers than genes (The ENCODE Project Consortium, 2012).
evidence: Supported by citation to The ENCODE Project Consortium, 2012

claim: Genes are frequently controlled by multiple enhancers.
source: Indeed, genes are frequently controlled by multiple enhancers (Shlyueva et al., 2014; Gasperini et al., 2020; Kim and Wysocka, 2023).

claim: Enhancers are often clustered and jointly regulate a nearby tissue-specific gene.
source: Often, such enhancers are clustered and jointly regulate a nearby tissue-specific gene (Tuan et al., 1985; Grosveld et al., 1987; Tolhuis et al., 2002; Deng et al., 2012; Hnisz et al., 2013; Whyte et al., 2013; Hay et al., 2016; Schoenfelder and Fraser, 2019; Brosh et al., 2023).

claim: Several studies have found that enhancers can combine either additively.
source: Several studies have found that enhancers can combine either additively (Bothma et al., 2015; Lam et al., 2015; Dukler et al., 2016; Hay et al., 2016; Will et al., 2017; Lin et al., 2022), supra-additively (indicating synergy) (Bothma et al., 2015; Lam et al., 2015; Joo et al., 2016; Shin et al., 2016; Carleton et al., 2017; Thomas et al., 2021; Lin et al., 2022; Brosh et al., 2023), or sub-additively (indicating redundance) (Moorthy et al., 2017; Osterwalder et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations to previous studies

claim: Enhancers can combine supra-additively (indicating synergy).
source: Several studies have found that enhancers can combine either additively (Bothma et al., 2015; Lam et al., 2015; Dukler et al., 2016; Hay et al., 2016; Will et al., 2017; Lin et al., 2022), supra-additively (indicating synergy) (Bothma et al., 2015; Lam et al., 2015; Joo et al., 2016; Shin et al., 2016; Carleton et al., 2017; Thomas et al., 2021; Lin et al., 2022; Brosh et al., 2023), or sub-additively (indicating redundance) (Moorthy et al., 2017; Osterwalder et al., 2018).

claim: Enhancers can combine sub-additively (indicating redundance).
source: Several studies have found that enhancers can combine either additively (Bothma et al., 2015; Lam et al., 2015; Dukler et al., 2016; Hay et al., 2016; Will et al., 2017; Lin et al., 2022), supra-additively (indicating synergy) (Bothma et al., 2015; Lam et al., 2015; Joo et al., 2016; Shin et al., 2016; Carleton et al., 2017; Thomas et al., 2021; Lin et al., 2022; Brosh et al., 2023), or sub-additively (indicating redundance) (Moorthy et al., 2017; Osterwalder et al., 2018).

claim: All previous studies on enhancer-enhancer interactions tested only small numbers of enhancers in one or a few genomic loci.
source: Nevertheless, all of these studies tested only small numbers of enhancers in one or a few genomic loci.
evidence: Statement about the scope of previous studies

claim: The study tested about 69,000 enhancer-enhancer-promoter combinations in mouse embryonic stem cells.
source: By testing about 69,000 EEP combinations in mouse embryonic stem cells (mESCs) we found that pairs of enhancers mostly combine near-additively.

claim: Pairs of enhancers mostly combine near-additively.
source: By testing about 69,000 EEP combinations in mouse embryonic stem cells (mESCs) we found that pairs of enhancers mostly combine near-additively.
evidence: Primary finding from the experimental data

claim: Promoter choice affects enhancer-enhancer interplay.
source: Furthermore, promoter choice affects this EE interplay, and promoters integrate the enhancer effects in a non-linear manner.

claim: Promoters integrate enhancer effects in a non-linear manner.
source: Furthermore, promoter choice affects this EE interplay, and promoters integrate the enhancer effects in a non-linear manner.

claim: The study designed a cloning strategy that enabled construction of libraries of tens of thousands of reporters that each contain a different EEP combination.
source: We designed a cloning strategy that enabled us to construct libraries of tens of thousands of reporters that each contain a different EEP combination (Figure 1A and B).
evidence: Description of experimental design with reference to Figure 1

claim: Eight barcoded reporter assay libraries were constructed, one per promoter.
source: Eight barcoded reporter assay libraries, one per promoter, were constructed.

claim: Seven of the eight promoters tested are from tightly regulated genes involved in the control of the pluripotency state of cells or their exit from this state.
source: Of these, seven are from tightly regulated genes that are involved in the control of the pluripotency state of the cells or their exit from this state (Klf2, Sox2, Nanog, Otx2, Lefty1, Ffg5, Tbx3) (Acampora et al., 2013; Dunn et al., 2014; Kim et al., 2014; Thomas et al., 2021).
evidence: Supported by citations and description of promoter selection

claim: The Ap1m1 promoter is from a housekeeping gene.
source: In addition, we included the promoter of the housekeeping (Hounkpe et al., 2021) gene Ap1m1, which neighbours the Klf2 gene.
evidence: Supported by citation to Hounkpe et al., 2021

claim: The study included approximately the −350 to +50 bp region around the transcription start site for each promoter.
source: From each promoter we approximately included the −350 to +50 bp region around the transcription start site (TSS), because this includes the most information-rich part of functional promoters (Martinez-Ara et al., 2022; van Arensbergen et al., 2017).
evidence: Supported by citations explaining the rationale

claim: The study selected 59 single enhancers.
source: In total we selected 59 of such single enhancers.
evidence: Direct statement of number of enhancers

claim: The study included 20 random sequences as negative controls.
source: We also included 20 random sequences as negative controls (see Methods, Supplementary file 2).

claim: The libraries covered 138,528 (69%) of the total combinatorial space.
source: Of this space, the libraries covered 138,528 (69%) of the total combinatorial space, and after application of stringent quality filters (see Methods) we were able to determine activities of 110,180 (55%) combinations (Supplementary file 3).

claim: After quality filters, the study determined activities of 110,180 (55%) combinations.
source: Of this space, the libraries covered 138,528 (69%) of the total combinatorial space, and after application of stringent quality filters (see Methods) we were able to determine activities of 110,180 (55%) combinations (Supplementary file 3).

claim: The study measured 2584 control-control combinations.
source: In total, we measured 2584 CC combinations, 38,390 EC combinations, and 69,206 EE combinations.

claim: The study measured 38,390 enhancer-control combinations.
source: In total, we measured 2584 CC combinations, 38,390 EC combinations, and 69,206 EE combinations.

claim: The study measured 69,206 enhancer-enhancer combinations.
source: In total, we measured 2584 CC combinations, 38,390 EC combinations, and 69,206 EE combinations.

claim: All developmental promoter libraries showed high correlations between replicates (Pearson's R=0.82–0.96).
source: For these averaged activities, all developmental promoter libraries showed high correlations between replicates (Pearson's R=0.82–0.96) (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Direct statement with reference to Figure 2—figure supplement 1

claim: The housekeeping promoter library showed somewhat lower correlations between replicates (Pearson's R=0.74–0.78).
source: The housekeeping promoter library showed somewhat lower correlations between replicates (Pearson's R=0.74–0.78), which is most likely due to a smaller dynamic range.

claim: There was little position and orientation dependence of the enhancer effects.
source: We observed that there was little position and orientation dependence of the enhancer effects (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: Direct observation with reference to Figure 2—figure supplement 2

claim: The majority of the sequences selected as enhancers indeed act as enhancers.
source: The single enhancer boost indices show that the majority of the sequences that we selected indeed act as enhancers, although the boost indices varied up to ~5 log2 units (Figure 2A and B).
evidence: Direct statement with reference to Figure 2

claim: All tested enhancers showed significant activation of at least one promoter (at an estimated false discovery rate [FDR]<0.01).
source: All tested enhancers showed significant activation of at least one promoter (at an estimated false discovery rate [FDR]<0.01) (Figure 2B and D).
evidence: Direct statement with statistical threshold and reference to Figure 2

claim: The boost indices are particularly smaller for the housekeeping promoter (Ap1m1).
source: However, the dynamic ranges and effects of each enhancer vary per promoter, with the boost indices being particularly smaller for the housekeeping promoter (Ap1m1) (Figure 2A and C).
evidence: Direct observation with reference to Figure 2

claim: The majority of tested enhancers exhibited significant preference for certain promoters.
source: In our previous study of a large set of E-P pairs we found that the majority of tested enhancers exhibited significant preference for certain promoters (Martinez-Ara et al., 2022). Applying the same statistical analysis to the current enhancer set confirmed this finding: the variability of enhancer effects across promoters are generally larger than what is expected from experimental noise (Figure 2—figure supplement 3).
evidence: Confirmed by statistical analysis with reference to previous study and Figure 2—figure supplement 3

claim: The single enhancers tested show significant promoter selectivity.
source: This indicates that the single enhancers tested here show significant promoter selectivity.

claim: Enhancer-enhancer combinations generally were more active than enhancer-control combinations.
source: In the boost index matrix that covers all combinations for a single promoter, we observed that generally EE combinations were more active than EC combinations (Figure 3A).
evidence: Direct observation with reference to Figure 3A

claim: Enhancer-enhancer combinations tend to induce stronger activation than single enhancers.
source: Indeed, quantitative analysis showed that EE combinations tend to induce stronger activation than the single enhancers (EC) (Figure 3B and C), although some saturation appears to occur with the strongest enhancers (Figure 3C).
evidence: Quantitative analysis with reference to Figure 3

claim: Some saturation appears to occur with the strongest enhancers.
source: Indeed, quantitative analysis showed that EE combinations tend to induce stronger activation than the single enhancers (EC) (Figure 3B and C), although some saturation appears to occur with the strongest enhancers (Figure 3C).
evidence: Observation from quantitative analysis with reference to Figure 3C

claim: For most of the promoters the additive model consistently showed a better fit to the measured data than the multiplicative model.
source: Interestingly, for most of the promoters the additive model consistently showed a better fit to the measured data than the multiplicative model (Figure 3E and F, Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Comparison of models with reference to figures

claim: The multiplicative model tended to strongly overestimate activities at the higher range of activities for most promoters.
source: In particular, the multiplicative model tended to strongly overestimate activities at the higher range of activities (most active enhancers) for most promoters.

claim: For the Ap1m1 promoter the multiplicative and additive models were nearly indistinguishable.
source: Only for the Ap1m1 promoter the multiplicative and additive models were nearly indistinguishable.

claim: A simple additive model fits the observed data better than a multiplicative model.
source: In summary, we conclude that a simple additive model fits the observed data better than a multiplicative model.

claim: 74.5% of the measured enhancer-enhancer activities lies within one standard deviation of the predicted activities according to the additive model.
source: By applying a simple error model to estimate the noise in the expected EE activities according to the additive model (Figure 3D, see Methods) we found that 74.5% of the measured EE activities lies within one standard deviation (SD) of the predicted activities (Figure 4A) and 94% lies within two SD.
evidence: Statistical analysis with reference to Figure 3D and 4A

claim: 94% of measured enhancer-enhancer activities lies within two standard deviations of the predicted activities according to the additive model.
source: By applying a simple error model to estimate the noise in the expected EE activities according to the additive model (Figure 3D, see Methods) we found that 74.5% of the measured EE activities lies within one standard deviation (SD) of the predicted activities (Figure 4A) and 94% lies within two SD.
evidence: Statistical analysis with reference to figures

claim: Most of the tested enhancers combine near-additively.
source: This underscores that most of the tested enhancers combine near-additively, and that both sub-additive and supra-additive effects are generally rare or weak.

claim: Both sub-additive and supra-additive effects are generally rare or weak.
source: This underscores that most of the tested enhancers combine near-additively, and that both sub-additive and supra-additive effects are generally rare or weak.

claim: The Sox2, Lefty1, Tbx3, and Fgf5 promoters showed a relatively large proportion of enhancer-enhancer pairs with supra-additive effects.
source: The Sox2, Lefty1, Tbx3, and Fgf5 promoters showed a relatively large proportion of EE pairs with supra-additive effects, while the Ap1m1 promoter exhibited the lowest frequency of supra-additivity.

claim: The Ap1m1 promoter exhibited the lowest frequency of supra-additivity.
source: The Sox2, Lefty1, Tbx3, and Fgf5 promoters showed a relatively large proportion of EE pairs with supra-additive effects, while the Ap1m1 promoter exhibited the lowest frequency of supra-additivity.

claim: The proportion of supra-additivity correlates inversely with promoter baseline expression.
source: Interestingly, the proportion of supra-additivity correlates inversely with promoter baseline expression (Figure 4B, left panel).
evidence: Statistical correlation with reference to Figure 4B

claim: Lowly active promoters allow more supra-additive enhancer-enhancer interactions, although these remain a minority (<40% of enhancer-enhancer pairs).
source: Thus, lowly active promoters allow more supra-additive EE interactions, although these remain a minority (<40% of EE pairs).

claim: The proportion of sub-additive effects is very similar across promoters.
source: In contrast, the proportion of sub-additive effects (i.e. >1 SD below expected activity) is very similar across promoters (Figure 4B, right).
evidence: Direct observation with reference to Figure 4B

claim: There is no strong saturation effect that could explain the decrease in number of supra-additive interactions as promoter activity increases.
source: This latter observation suggests that there is no strong saturation effect that could explain the decrease in number of supra-additive interactions as promoter activity increases.
evidence: Inference from observation about sub-additive effects

claim: Out of the 58 tested enhancers 32.7% (19/58) showed consistent supra-additivity in at least one promoter context.
source: Out of the 58 tested enhancers 32.7% (19/58) showed consistent supra-additivity in at least one promoter context (>0.5 log2(observed/expected), mean over all enhancers in at least one promoter context), and only 10.3% (6/58) showed consistent supra-additivity in two or more promoter contexts (Figure 4C).
evidence: Quantitative analysis with reference to Figure 4C

claim: Only 10.3% (6/58) of tested enhancers showed consistent supra-additivity in two or more promoter contexts.
source: Out of the 58 tested enhancers 32.7% (19/58) showed consistent supra-additivity in at least one promoter context (>0.5 log2(observed/expected), mean over all enhancers in at least one promoter context), and only 10.3% (6/58) showed consistent supra-additivity in two or more promoter contexts (Figure 4C).
evidence: Quantitative analysis with reference to Figure 4C

claim: Enhancer-enhancer combinations from the same locus showed on average not a higher observed/expected ratio than enhancer-enhancer combinations from different loci.
source: However, we found that EE combinations from the same locus showed on average not a higher observed/expected ratio (according to the additive model) than EE combinations from different loci; in fact, this ratio is even slightly lower (Figure 4E).
evidence: Direct comparison with reference to Figure 4E

claim: Generally there appears to be no preferential synergy among enhancers that are located in the same genomic locus.
source: Thus, generally there appears to be no preferential synergy among enhancers that are located in the same genomic locus.
evidence: Conclusion from comparison of within-locus vs between-locus combinations

claim: All seven developmental promoters showed strong pairwise correlations of their boost indices (Pearson's R=0.79–0.98).
source: Strikingly, all seven developmental promoters showed strong pairwise correlations of their boost indices (Pearson's R=0.79–0.98), whereas the housekeeping promoter (Ap1m1) correlated much less with each of the developmental promoters (Pearson's R=0.19–0.60; Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Statistical correlation analysis with reference to Figure 5—figure supplement 1

claim: The housekeeping promoter (Ap1m1) correlated much less with each of the developmental promoters (Pearson's R=0.19–0.60).
source: Strikingly, all seven developmental promoters showed strong pairwise correlations of their boost indices (Pearson's R=0.79–0.98), whereas the housekeeping promoter (Ap1m1) correlated much less with each of the developmental promoters (Pearson's R=0.19–0.60; Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Statistical correlation analysis with reference to Figure 5—figure supplement 1

claim: All of the developmental promoters correlated strongly with the average boost index pattern (Pearson's R=0.93–0.99).
source: All of the developmental promoters correlated strongly with this average pattern (Pearson's R=0.93–0.99) but this was not the case for the housekeeping promoter (Pearson's R=0.42).

claim: The housekeeping promoter did not correlate strongly with the average boost index pattern (Pearson's R=0.42).
source: All of the developmental promoters correlated strongly with this average pattern (Pearson's R=0.93–0.99) but this was not the case for the housekeeping promoter (Pearson's R=0.42).

claim: The slopes relative to the averaged promoters ranged from 1.54 to 0.32, i.e., about fivefold, across the developmental promoters.
source: The slopes relative to the averaged promoters ranged from 1.54 to 0.32, i.e., about fivefold, across the developmental promoters.

claim: The developmental promoters differ in the scaling (i.e. steepness) of their responses to the set of enhancer-enhancer pairs, even though the pattern of their responses is highly similar.
source: These results imply that the developmental promoters differ in the scaling (i.e. steepness) of their responses to the set of EE pairs, even though the pattern of their responses is highly similar.

claim: The relative slopes negatively correlate with the baseline activity of the developmental promoters.
source: Interestingly, the relative slopes negatively correlate with the baseline activity of these promoters (Figure 5B).
evidence: Statistical correlation with reference to Figure 5B

claim: Promoters with low intrinsic activity respond more steeply to changes in combined enhancer-enhancer activity than promoters with high intrinsic activity.
source: Thus, promoters with low intrinsic activity respond more steeply to changes in combined EE activity than promoters with high intrinsic activity.

claim: Differential responses of promoters can also be observed with single enhancer elements.
source: Finally, we asked whether these differential responses of promoters require EE pairs, or can also be observed with single E elements. Indeed, this is the case (Figure 5—figure supplement 2).
evidence: Analysis with reference to Figure 5—figure supplement 2

claim: The study is of a much larger scale than previous efforts to elucidate the combinatorial interplay among enhancers.
source: Here, we employed an MPRA approach to measure three-way regulatory interactions in ~69,000 EEP combinations involving 8 promoters and 59 enhancers. This is of a much larger scale than previous efforts to elucidate the combinatorial interplay among enhancers, which typically focused on a handful of enhancers in single genomic loci (Bothma et al., 2015; Hay et al., 2016; Shin et al., 2016; Dukler et al., 2016; Joo et al., 2016; Lam et al., 2015; Carleton et al., 2017; Moorthy et al., 2017; Osterwalder et al., 2018; Thomas et al., 2021; Lin et al., 2022; Brosh et al., 2023).

claim: Previous studies pointed to a diversity of functional enhancer-enhancer interactions, including redundancy, additivity, and synergy.
source: These previous studies pointed to a diversity of functional EE interactions, including redundancy, additivity, and synergy.

claim: The current study uncovered a broad spectrum of functional interactions, but simple near-additive effects of enhancer-enhancer combinations were predominant.
source: Our study also uncovered a broad spectrum of functional interactions, but simple near-additive effects of EE combinations were predominant, while supra-additive interactions occurred at a lower frequency and were dependent on the specific enhancer and promoter context.

claim: Supra-additive interactions occurred at a lower frequency and were dependent on the specific enhancer and promoter context.
source: Our study also uncovered a broad spectrum of functional interactions, but simple near-additive effects of EE combinations were predominant, while supra-additive interactions occurred at a lower frequency and were dependent on the specific enhancer and promoter context.

claim: Promoters can have substantial impact on supra-additivity of enhancer-enhancer interactions.
source: An important finding is that promoters can have substantial impact on supra-additivity of EE interactions.

claim: Promoters may be seen as 'interpreters' of enhancer-enhancer combinations.
source: Promoters may thus be seen as 'interpreters' of EE combinations.

claim: The different promoters show different degrees of responsiveness to enhancer-enhancer pairs, with the stronger promoters being boosted less than the weaker promoters.
source: A salient finding is that the different promoters show different degrees of responsiveness to EE pairs, with the stronger promoters being boosted less than the weaker promoters.

claim: The responses of the promoters follow roughly a power-law function of which the exponent is dependent on the promoter.
source: The responses of the promoters follow roughly a power-law function of which the exponent is dependent on the promoter (Figure 5A and Figure 5—figure supplement 2, which are on log-log scale).

claim: The apparent saturation observable at high enhancer activities suggests that the exponents are most likely below 1.
source: The apparent saturation observable at high enhancer activities in Figure 3C suggests that the exponents are most likely below 1.

claim: The findings resemble those of an earlier study indicating that promoter activities are non-linearly scaled by the genomic environment, with the steepness of the scaling being negatively correlated with promoter strength.
source: Our findings resemble those of an earlier study (Hong and Cohen, 2022), indicating that promoter activities are non-linearly scaled by the genomic environment, with the steepness of the scaling being negatively correlated with promoter strength.

claim: The reporters in the MPRA were not integrated into the genome.
source: The reporters in our MPRA were not integrated into the genome.

claim: Testing all enhancer-enhancer-promoter combinations under similar conditions ensures no confounding effects of variable chromatin contexts.
source: On the one hand, this ensures that all EEP combinations are tested under similar conditions, without confounding effects of variable chromatin contexts.

claim: Other studies have indicated that transiently transfected reporters generally behave quite similar, although not identically, to integrated reporters.
source: However, other studies have indicated that transiently transfected reporters generally behave quite similar, although not identically, to integrated reporters (Inoue and Ahituv, 2015; Klein et al., 2020), and another study indicated that chromatin context can scale transcriptional activity of inserted reporters in a simple linear manner that is largely independent of the inserted sequence (Maricque et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous studies

claim: The results may be biased by the selection of enhancers and promoters, which was mostly focused on genes linked to pluripotency in mouse ESCs.
source: We cannot rule out that our results are biased by our selection of enhancers and promoters, which was mostly focused on genes linked to pluripotency in mouse ESCs.

claim: The protocol developed for three-way MPRAs should be generally applicable to any set of enhancers and promoters.
source: However, the protocol that we developed for three-way MPRAs should be generally applicable to any set of enhancers and promoters.

claim: In the MPRA the enhancer and promoter elements are placed in fixed positions and close to one another, which does not recapitulate their relative positioning in the genome.
source: It should also be considered that in our MPRA the enhancer and promoter elements are placed in fixed positions and close to one another, which does not recapitulate their relative positioning in the genome.

claim: Genomic distance and chromatin contexts could act as thresholds for activation, or turn additive interactions into non-linear relationships.
source: Genomic distance and chromatin contexts could act as thresholds for activation, or turn additive interactions into non-linear relationships.

claim: The ability of a Sox2 enhancer to activate its cognate promoter was found to depend on their distance, following a non-linear decay function.
source: For instance, the ability of a Sox2 enhancer to activate its cognate promoter was found to depend on their distance, following a non-linear decay function (Zuin et al., 2022).
evidence: Supported by citation to Zuin et al., 2022

claim: A recent report indicated that distant pairs of enhancers are more often synergistic than closely spaced enhancers, which tend to act additively.
source: The rules for EE interplay may depend on the EE distance or genomic context, as suggested by a recent report indicating that distant pairs of enhancers are more often synergistic than closely spaced enhancers, which tend to act additively (Lin et al., 2022).
evidence: Supported by citation to Lin et al., 2022

claim: A recent study reported synergies between enhancer elements in the Sox2 locus control region in the native genomic context.
source: A recent study reported synergies between E elements in the Sox2 locus control region (a large compound enhancer region) in the native genomic context (Brosh et al., 2023).
evidence: Supported by citation to Brosh et al., 2023

claim: The current study did not observe synergies in the Sox2 locus control region, but the data are not directly comparable due to differences in the size of the elements tested.
source: We did not observe such synergies, but the data of that study are not directly comparable to ours due to differences in the size of the elements tested.

claim: In the native Fgf5 locus, several of the enhancer elements exhibited some degree of synergy in differentiated cells.
source: In the native Fgf5 locus, several of the E elements exhibited some degree of synergy in differentiated cells (Thomas et al., 2021).
evidence: Supported by citation to Thomas et al., 2021

claim: In mESCs the synergy in the Fgf5 locus was not detected, which is in line with the current study's results for the same enhancer elements from the Fgf5 locus.
source: However, in mESCs this synergy was not detected, which is in line our results for the same E elements from the Fgf5 locus.
evidence: Comparison with previous study and current data

claim: The default mode of enhancer-enhancer interplay is additive, while the precise chromatin context, element spacing, and cellular state may enable synergy in some genomic loci.
source: Possibly, the default mode of EE interplay is additive, while the precise chromatin context, element spacing, and cellular state may enable synergy in some genomic loci.
evidence: Speculation based on comparison of findings

claim: In a previous MPRA study the authors found evidence for selectivity of enhancer-promoter functional interactions.
source: In our previous MPRA study (Martinez-Ara et al., 2022) we found evidence for selectivity of enhancer-promoter functional interactions (see definition of selectivity in Computational methods section).

claim: There are two intermingled factors that account for differences between promoters: distinct classes of promoters show different specificities, and promoters scale the input they receive from enhancer pairs differently.
source: The data from the eight promoters indicate that there are two intermingled factors that account for differences between promoters. First, distinct classes of promoters show different specificities, as illustrated by the poor correlations between the Ap1m1 housekeeping promoter and the developmental promoters. Second, promoters scale the input they receive from enhancer pairs differently, as discussed above.

claim: The compatibility differences observed in the previous study are a mix of promoters that respond differently to enhancers because of specificity, and promoters that respond differently to enhancers because of differences in responsiveness caused by their intrinsic strength.
source: It is probable that the compatibility differences we observed in our previous study (Martinez-Ara et al., 2022) are a mix of these two phenomena: (1) promoters that respond differently to enhancers because of specificity, and (2) promoters that respond differently to enhancers because of differences in responsiveness caused by their intrinsic strength.
evidence: Inference connecting current and previous findings

claim: The near-additivity of enhancers will help understand how different enhancers may be more or less relevant in different loci.
source: The near-additivity of enhancers will help us understand how different enhancers may be more or less relevant in different loci.

claim: The non-linearity of promoter responsiveness and the effects of promoters on enhancer-enhancer interactions illustrates how some promoters may be more sensitive to activating signals.
source: The non-linearity of promoter responsiveness and the effects of promoters on enhancer-enhancer interactions illustrates how some promoters may be more sensitive to activating signals.

claim: It will be useful to quantify promoter responsiveness genome-wide to understand which genes may be more or less sensitive than others to environmental cues or to non-coding mutations.
source: Thus, it will be useful to quantify promoter responsiveness genome-wide to understand which genes may be more or less sensitive than others to environmental cues or to non-coding mutations.

claim: Developmentally regulated transcription factors and their target genes can be very sensitive to dosage changes.
source: These aspects may be especially relevant for developmentally regulated transcription factors and their target genes, like the ones here studied, as they can be very sensitive to dosage changes (Naqvi et al., 2023).
evidence: Supported by citation to Naqvi et al., 2023

claim: E14tg2a male mESCs were used for all experiments.
source: We used E14tg2a male mESCs (ATCC CRL-1821) cultured in 2i+LIF for all experiments.

claim: Single enhancers were defined as ~400 bp elements overlapping with DNase hypersensitive sites in clusters of enhancers.
source: We defined single enhancers as ~400 bp elements overlapping with DNase hypersensitive sites (DHSs) in clusters of enhancers (Figure 1C and D), as previously described (Martinez-Ara et al., 2022).
evidence: Description of methods with reference to figures and previous study

claim: DHSs have been shown to retain enhancer activity individually.
source: However, since DHSs have been shown to retain enhancer activity individually (Barakat et al., 2018; Agrawal et al., 2021; Bergman et al., 2022; Martinez-Ara et al., 2022) we decided to test the combinatorial contributions of these smaller elements of an enhancer cluster.
